decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 3 - No above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until samples of all materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. - cladding details, - window treatment (including sections/reveals); - entrance doors and external door frames and any other materials/details to be used. 
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order that the Council may be satisfied as to the details of the development in the interests of the visual amenity of the area

Condition : 4 - a) The hereby approved development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Statement. 
b) Prior to first occupation of any building within the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and to include As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions, and achieved a 100% reduction in emissions. This shall also include details regarding capped connections provided for the prospective district heat network.
c) Prior to first occupation of the hereby approved development, where a contribution is found necessary to achieve compliance with zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the developer shall have entered into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay any carbon offset contribution at the published rate in-force at the time of submitting details pursuant to Part B of this condition. 
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions

Condition : 5 - The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of delivery notes, invoices or installation contracts) have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development meets the following: 
- At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
- No construction or insulation materials are to be used which will release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials

Condition : 6 - The development unless otherwise agreed in writing, shall achieve an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits under BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) for the Shell stage 
a)	Prior to the occupation, a BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) for the Shell pre-assessment report shall be submitted, by the developer, and approved in writing by the local planning authority to demonstrate how the creative workspace will achieve an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits.
b)	Within six months of first occupation, unless otherwise agreed in writing, a BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) for the Shell Final (Post - Construction) Certificate, issued by the BRE (or equivalent accredited body), must be submitted by the developer, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as the development is in existence. 
Reason: To ensure a sustainable development.

Condition : 7 - Prior to commencement of any development, an updated detailed air quality assessment assessing operational and construction phase impacts must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The updated detailed air quality assessment must address all London Borough of Hounslow comments made on the previous assessment.  The updated air quality assessment must be carried out in accordance with all new and updated relevant policy and guidance documents at the time of writing, as well as using the most up to date Defra tools (such as EFT and NOX to NO2) and 2021 reference year background maps. 
Reason: In the interests of air quality and to protect neighbours' living conditions and the wider local environment.

Condition : 8 - a)	Prior to erection of the buildings on site a scheme of sound insulation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority as necessary to achieve the relevant internal noise level criteria as specified in 'Building bulletin 93 - Acoustic design of schools: performance standards' (BB93). 

b)	Prior to first occupation of any building used for teaching or learning, validation testing should be carried out, and results approved by the Local Planning Authority, to demonstrate that suitable internal ambient noise levels in accordance with BB93 have been achieved on site. The testing should be carried out in accordance with the latest version of 'ANC Good Practice Guide - Acoustic Testing of Schools'.
Any remedial measures to achieve the BB93 internal noise level criteria should be installed prior to the validation testing and thereafter be permanently retained whilst the building is used for teaching or learning purposes on site.
Reason: In the interest of providing acceptable internal conditions for the occupants of the development.

Condition : 9 - Based upon guidance contained within BS 5228:2009 + A1:2014: Noise, Noise levels from construction works at nearby existing and proposed residential receptors shall not exceed the following construction noise criteria:
Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst-affected residential property during the following time periods:
�	Monday to Friday (08:00 � 18:00 hours) 	 
�	Saturday (08:00 to 13:00 hours)
Works outside of the standard hours will be subject to prior agreement and prior notice will be provided to the London Borough of Hounslow.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 10 - The cumulative noise from any fixed external plant associated with the scheme should not exceed levels more than 10 dB below representative background (LA90) levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby existing and proposed dwellings, over any period that the plant is operational. Noise levels should be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS4142: 2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance.
Reason: In order to ensure that occupants of the development and its neighbours are not exposed to unreasonable levels of fixed plant noise.

Condition : 11 - (a)	Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the submitted Flood Risk and Drainage Assessment and associated drawings. The drainage assessment must be revised to follow the London Plan drainage hierarchy which prioritises rainwater harvesting and green infrastructure. The calculations must also be revised to show that FEH22 rainfall data has been used, the correct storage volumes are demonstrated, and to show suitable half-drain times. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.

(b)	No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, the National Planning Policy Framework (Paragraph 103), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 12 - The development shall not be occupied until confirmation is provided that either:
1. All necessary upgrades to the foul water network to accommodate additional flows from the development have been completed; or
2. A phasing plan for development and infrastructure, agreed with Thames Water and the Local Planning Authority, is in place. Where such a plan exists, no occupation shall occur other than in accordance with the approved phasing schedule.

Reason: Network reinforcement is likely to be required to support the proposed development. These upgrades are essential to avoid the risk of sewer flooding and pollution incidents.

Condition : 14 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Car Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following:

(i)	details of parking allocations for various users of the approved development and how this will be operated and enforced
(ii)	details of measures proposed to restrict parking to designated bays only and prohibit parking on the access road
(iii)	a commitment to convert passive EV bays to active when demand requires.
(iv)	details of the operation of any gates or barriers
(v)	measures to ensure that all prospective users are informed of the Parking Management Plan 
The parking areas and access road(s) shall thereafter be managed in compliance with the approved Car Parking Management Plan, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to secure any variation.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.

Condition : 15 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery & Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 16 - Prior to the first use or occupation of the development full details (including manufacturers' specifications) of secure covered cycle parking facilities, that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the development is first occupied or brought into use. The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 18 - Notwithstanding the details submitted, no development shall take place (including vegetation clearance, demolition, and ground works) until a Construction Environment Management Plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Plan shall include: 
a)	Identification of stages of works, details of working hours
b)	Risk assessment and mitigation measures for construction traffic, noise and vibration, dust and air pollutants, land contamination, ecology and ground water. 
c)	Setting up of site- protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs
d)	Details of the ecological clerk of works or responsible person and lines of communication, 
e)	Watching brief for bats, birds, reptiles and amphibians including details of the pre-development checks, and, identified on maps where applicable, measures to mitigate the impacts of construction activities on wildlife, construction lighting plan, and details of any licensing requirement
f)	Protocol for non-native invasive species, unexpected fauna if encountered on site
g)	Communication with the neighbouring residents in order to safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area in general.

The approved CEMP should be followed and implemented throughout the construction period in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat and secure opportunities for the enhancement of the nature conservation value of the site.

Condition : 20 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall  be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include; (a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat, (b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development, (e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and (f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years. 
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 21 - Notwithstanding the submitted details, no above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until a habitat management plan in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The habitat management plan shall include:
a)	Prescription for management actions.
b)	Preparation of the work schedule (including an annual work Plan for over 30-year period and who will carry out the jobs mentioned in the management plans).
c)	Details of the body or organisation responsible for implementation of the plan.
d)	Time frame for reviewing the plan.
e)	Details of the management plans and its communication to the occupiers of the development.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 22 - a)	Prior to first occupation, the two relocated basketball courts shall have been constructed in accordance with approved drawing SRP1143-ONE-ZZ-XX-D-L-0002-P14, and the facility shall be retained for use thereafter.
b)	Any amendments to the above scheme shall be approved in writing from the Local Planning Authority and be made available for use before the development is first occupied or brought into use. The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use at all times.
Reason: To ensure adequate facilities have been provided within the development.

Condition : 23 - The outdoor playing pitches and MUGA courts within the Main school campus and its associated sports lighting shall not be used outside of the hours of:
�	Monday to Friday 8:30-15:00hrs
�	No use on Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays/public holidays 

The Sport Lighting should be switched off when the MUGA is not in use, and within 30 minutes at the end of the permitted hours of use.

Reason: To balance illuminating the outdoor playing field/sports facility for maximum use and benefit to sport with the interest of amenity and sustainability

Condition : 24 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 25 - During the development:
The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 26 - Prior to the development being first brought into use:
The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 27 - If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the local planning authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice.
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice.
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.

Condition : 28 - No above-ground development shall commence until a Bird Hazard Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted plan shall include details of:
- Management of any flat/shallow pitched/green roofs on buildings within the site which may be attractive to nesting, roosting and "loafing" birds. 
The Bird Hazard Management Plan shall be implemented as approved and shall remain in force for the life of the buildings. No subsequent alterations to the plan are to take place unless first submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.
Information
The Bird Hazard Management Plan must ensure that flat/shallow pitched roofs be constructed to allow access to all areas by foot using permanent fixed access stairs ladders or similar. The owner/occupier must not allow gulls, to nest, roost or loaf on the building. Checks must be made weekly or sooner if bird activity dictates, during the breeding season. Outside of the breeding season gull activity must be monitored and the roof checked regularly to ensure that gulls do not utilise the roof.  Any gulls found nesting, roosting or loafing must be dispersed by the owner/occupier when detected or when requested by Heathrow Airside Operations staff. In some instances, it may be necessary to contact Heathrow Airside Operations staff before bird dispersal takes place. The owner/occupier must remove any nests or eggs found on the roof. The breeding season for gulls typically runs from March to June. The owner/occupier must obtain the appropriate licences where applicable from Natural England before the removal of nests and eggs.

Condition : 29 - No solar panels shall be installed until a glint and glare assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No subsequent alterations to the approved scheme are to take place unless submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure the development does not endanger the safe movement of aircraft or the operation of Heathrow Airport. The airport requires a glint and glare assessment to be completed to determine the full impact on Air Traffic Control Tower and pilots approaching the airport.

Condition : 30 - Prior to occupation the development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO).
Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998

Condition : 31 - At least six months prior to occupation, a night-time assessment for the Active Travel Zone shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Transport for London. The submitted details must objectively assess the agreed routes around the school site, and identify appropriate mitigation measures that may be required to  ensure that the surrounding infrastructure complies with Healthy Street Indicators" 
Reason- In the interest of safe and sustainable transport objectives
